obernants.assumptions: Source/sink and all vertex IDs must retain coordinates across joins. Allocation failure is outside typed errors. MCS/core reject invalid endpoints, loops, duplicate neighbors and asymmetry. Dominators allows loops/duplicates and validates caps then start/endpoints. Reduction normalizes duplicates and rejects every directed cycle.

obernants.operator: Exclude flow witnesses violating capacity, conservation, exact sum of cost*flow or capped lexicographic optimum; MCS orders violating prefix priority/ties; cores omitting feasible induced subsets; dominator membership contradicted by an avoiding path; or reductions with changed closure/redundant retained edges. Exclude invalid directedness joins, wrapping checked arithmetic and treating rejected negative cycles as zero-cost empty output.

obernants.operator: Empty and complete simple graphs both yield ascending MCS order. At k=1 a three-vertex path and triangle both yield all vertices. Adding loops to a directed chain preserves its dominator sets; adding any subset of reachable pairs to a reduced DAG preserves its reduction. Flow value/cost/witness admits changes to unused capacities/costs that preserve optimality. Thus neither the aggregate result nor these individual projections reconstructs a unique original graph.

obernants.operator: For a directed acyclic graph with unit capacities and unit costs and distinct reachable terminals, requested flow1 has value1 and cost equal to the shortest source-sink edge count. If sink is unreachable, value0 and cost0 require a separate reachability tag. This relation does not extend to arbitrary weighted flow, negative cycles, or larger flow limits.

obernants.operator: For reachable v, d is in Dom(v) iff deleting d destroys start-to-v reachability, counting removal of start as reaching nothing. Start and v belong to each reachable Dom(v). obernants.operator: core_k is the union of all induced vertex subsets of minimum degree>=k; union preserves feasibility. Consequently core_l subset core_k for k<=l, adding a simple undirected edge cannot shrink a core, and peeling the returned induced graph again deletes nothing.
